question_en: First-time sailing group asks which boat suits them (offer sent covered monohulls and catamarans, with skipper). Offer sent by us on 2026-01-20; sailing week 29.08.2026 to 05.09.2026.
answer_exact: Our fleet consists of monohulls, the authentic sailing boats, and catamarans, which usually have more amenities than monohulls and offer a more relaxed experience. Because you're an active crew, a monohull will provide a more engaging experience, perfect for learning the fundamentals and introducing you to sailing. That said, below you will find our offer including both monohulls and catamarans. The ultimate choice is up to you!

question_en: Client asks for the skipper fee and what it includes (implicit in offer; skipper discussed).
answer_exact: The skipper fee is €1,400, excluding his food. This means you can either include him in your meal plan or provide a daily allowance for him to arrange his own meals. We recommend that he has his own cabin so he can rest and everyone has privacy.

question_en: What are the mandatory extras, insurance and deposit? (price breakdown given for Oceanis 51.1 example)
answer_exact: Mandatory extras: Cleaning fee 350 €. The cleaning fee is the only obligatory extra we have. It includes bed linen, body and face towel, pillowcases as well as the final cleaning of the boat. Damage waiver: 480 €. This covers the insurance. Apart from the above mentioned cost there is also a 1.200 € amount that is refundable and settled with a pre-authorization to your credit or debit card.

question_en: Is the outboard / SUP included, and how does fuel work?
answer_exact: Outboard engine: 90 EUR. This extra is highly recommended by us as it would be very useful during your trip. It is the motor engine of the dinghy. The tender is included in the price however the outboard has an extra charge. SUP: 130 EUR. Last but not least, let me inform you regarding the fuel. The boat will be given to you with a full tank and after you return you only have to settle the fuel you have spent.

question_en: Client prefers a catamaran (Bali 4.1 Ramon) and asks for a floor plan, further information and any further discount.
answer_exact: Our Ramon - Bali 4.1 is a fantastic yacht, offering features that make your trip truly enjoyable. The spacious family-sized fridges allow you to store plenty of groceries, which is very convenient during your journey. The aft deck and saloon can be fully connected through a sliding door, creating a large open space where everyone can relax together, and there is also an additional forward saloon, providing another comfortable area for everyone to enjoy. Please find attached the layout of the yacht for your reference. ... To make your on-board experience even more enjoyable, we are pleased to offer you a complimentary SUP!

question_en: Do we have to pay a daily tourist tax per person on a boat?
answer_exact: It is not necessary to pay any daily tourist tax. In general, VAT is already included in the yacht price.

question_en: Roughly how much do people spend on fuel per week?
answer_exact: The yacht is handed over to you with full fuel. Refueling is done directly at our base, where we have a fuel truck available for your convenience, as lines at the marina can often be very long. Fuel costs, depending on your route, generally do not exceed €240 per week for larger catamarans like the Bali 4.2.

question_en: Skipper meals: if we give a daily allowance, how much should it be? Do we get a choice of skipper?
answer_exact: If you eat on board, one meal should also be considered for the skipper. If you dine ashore, you can either provide a daily allowance or invite the skipper to join you for meals, the choice is entirely yours and completely respected. All the skippers we work with are professional and have many years of experience, with excellent knowledge of the area. Most importantly, they all meet the high standards of IonianSails. To ensure we find the best possible match for our guests, we profile each skipper carefully. You will have plenty of time to meet him/her on the check-in day, and if there is anything you would like us to inform them about beforehand, please feel free to let us know.

question_en: Average mooring fees for a week? Do you offer airport transfers to and from Preveza airport and at what price?
answer_exact: If you need to dock at a port, charges vary depending on the port (usually €10-15). Marina fees are higher, but in any case, this depends on your plans and your arrangements with the skipper. One option is to anchor offshore and use the dinghy to reach the port. Of course, we can arrange your transfers. About two weeks before your charter, we will send you the attached transfer form. You complete it and pay the driver directly. The form also includes detailed pricing for your reference.

question_en: Ionian Islands or Split (Croatia): which would be better for us and why?
answer_exact: Between the two destinations you are considering, both countries offer stunning scenery and beautiful beaches. More specifically, although Croatia is a beautiful destination, our recent feedback is that, while it has always been more expensive, port fees have increased significantly in recent years. The Ionian Islands, on the other hand, offer calm and warm waters, unique nature with lush green islands, and plenty of bays where you can anchor and enjoy privacy, avoiding crowded marinas. This makes for a truly relaxing and authentic sailing experience.

question_en: Client confirms the group wants to go ahead and asks to confirm the booking (after a 5-day non-binding option was placed).
answer_exact: I will get back to you with the booking documents in a separate email, shortly. In the meantime, if you need any further information or assistance, please do not hesitate to contact us.

answer_exact: Yes, the security deposit is 1200 eur with a non-refundable damage waiver. As soon as we receive the payment, we will let you know:)

I have made a note that you will issue your commission invoice once the second payment is made. Please make sure you issue the invoice to the boat ownership details, which in this case are: [owner company name, address and tax number].

statement: Sun Odyssey 490 Kalm: monohull, 2020, Lefkas, 47 ft, 12 berths, 5 cabins, A/C, solar panels, generator, full batten mainsail. Atman Oceanis 51.1 offered as example: air conditioning in every cabin and a generator, so A/C can be used throughout the yacht, important during hot August days. Bali 4.1 Ramon: family-sized fridges, aft deck and saloon connected by sliding door, additional forward saloon.

Selling points used: privately held yachts in excellent condition thanks to winter maintenance in our own private shipyard; catamarans usually have more amenities than monohulls and a more relaxed experience; monohull is more engaging for beginners learning the fundamentals.

Direct client offer 29.08 to 05.09.2026: Sun Odyssey 490 Kalm list 6,800 EUR, special week discount -33% = 4,556 EUR, extra IonionSails discount -5% = 4,328 EUR. Oceanis 51.1 Atman yacht fee 5,540 EUR (example).

Non-binding option for direct client placed for 5 days, described as a pre-booking process to secure the preferred yacht. Complimentary SUP offered when client moves toward booking (Bali 4.1 Ramon, Jan 2026).
No daily tourist tax on boats. VAT generally already included in the yacht price.

January 2026 offer (Oceanis 51.1): damage waiver 480 EUR (covers the insurance) plus a refundable 1,200 EUR amount settled with a pre-authorization on credit or debit card. Cleaning fee 350 EUR is the only obligatory extra (includes bed linen, towels, pillowcases and final cleaning).

Skipper fee 1,400 EUR excluding food (Jan 2026, 2026 season); 1,470 EUR ex provisioning (Aug 2026 offer for 2027); 1,680 EUR and hostess 1,680 EUR on a crewed Saba 50 charter paid in cash on arrival (Aug 2026). Skipper meals: if eating on board, one meal also for the skipper; ashore, daily allowance or invite him. Crew meals are included in crew fee on crewed charters.

Airport transfers: transfer form sent about two weeks before charter; client completes it and pays the driver directly; pricing is in the form. Fuel: boat handed over full; refuel at our base with a fuel truck; fuel generally not above 240 EUR per week for larger catamarans. Mooring in ports usually 10 to 15 EUR; marinas higher. Fuel for the two-week 1a Yachtcharter case: 166 litres, 385 EUR.

Aura 51 week of 29 Aug 2026 (booked via partner Bax Yachting): client price 15,600.00 EUR (partner gross with extra 5% was 17,100.00 EUR per our message). Total charter fee shown by partner 14,036.58 EUR in a payment check, with two payments of 7,018.29 EUR (20 Jan) and 6,643.07 EUR (4 Aug). Figures differ between messages - needs confirmation.
Aura 51 offer (January 2026): a 3,500 EUR security deposit had been offered to the client.
Bali 4.1 'Theros' booking via broker (19/09-03/10/2026): security deposit is 1,200 EUR with a non-refundable damage waiver.

Broker flow: the broker's client paid the first payment (deposit) directly to IonionSails and the broker issues the commission invoice after the second payment, made out to the boat ownership company. We ask the broker to also confirm to the guest that the payment reached us. The broker sent the second payment proof and commission invoice on 14 Aug 2026 and asked for the crew list form.
